title: Audit current pipeline against the full-send readiness gate
doing: Perform a source/receipt-only gap audit of live simulator carry-over, scheduler/normalizer/averaging checkpoint state, full per-update PPO telemetry, evaluation isolation, fresh-stream exclusions, clocks and strict lifecycle. Compare generic code with the actual DODGE-013 journal path; no model loading, fixtures, games or training.
expected: Source-informed expectation: fresh-env checkpointing abandons live games, generic PPO computes some required metrics that the formal worker drops, and scheduler/full-state restore support is incomplete. Existing learner/RNG and strict resource/exact-once controls should be reusable, but source preparation cannot qualify the new long run.
actual: Source-only audit confirms fresh-env checkpointing abandons live games; formal recovery explicitly lacks full simulator state. Generic PPO computes numerical KL/entropy/value/EV/clip metrics, but formal update rows discard them. Fixed-LR guards, missing full-state/scheduler checkpoints, terminal evaluator global-RNG reseeding and unqualified I/O/resource costs block a robust long run. No games, model loads, optimizer steps or runtime qualification occurred.
why: The existing strict campaign was a terminal comparison, not a resumable long-run pipeline. Reuse its lifecycle components in a separately reviewed successor; do not weaken frozen guards.
next_step: Prepare full native/wrapper/learner state, schedule-aware guards, complete telemetry and isolated evaluation; qualify exact continuation and full-path resources before explicit launch approval.

evidence.label: Thirteen source-pinned readiness findings; not runtime qualification
User-directed long-run gate; no launch authority
